name: Lead magnet that loses money
story: The trial video pulls four times the leads of the carousel, but its few $49 sales do not cover its spend while the $99 carousel is very profitable.

why.trial_video: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $147.00; contribution = 147.00 x 0.70 - 147.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $97.03 vs spend $150 -> net -$52.97 (0.65 contribution per ad dollar). 40 leads look great, but on 3 counted orders it returns well under a dollar per ad dollar, so cut it (reduce, or pause until the lead-to-sale step is fixed); never increase on lead volume.
why.parent_carousel: 5 payments -> 5 counted orders, paid revenue $495.00; contribution = 495.00 x 0.70 - 495.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 5 = $329.25 vs spend $80 -> net +$249.25 (4.12 contribution per ad dollar). Five clean orders and about four dollars of contribution per ad dollar: the clear place to move budget.

name: Revenue per dollar above 1 but still losing
story: The free guide brings $1.17 of revenue per ad dollar, which looks profitable until the 30% teaching cost and PayPal fees are taken out.

why.free_guide: 6 payments -> 6 counted orders, paid revenue $234.00; contribution = 234.00 x 0.70 - 234.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 6 = $153.86 vs spend $200 -> net -$46.14 (0.77 contribution per ad dollar). Revenue/spend is 1.17, but break-even after the 30% cost and fees needs about 1.5, so it loses money: cut it.
why.holiday_static: 4 payments -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $316.00; contribution = 316.00 x 0.70 - 316.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $209.79 vs spend $100 -> net +$109.79 (2.10 contribution per ad dollar). Four clean $79 orders return about two dollars per ad dollar; increase is the best use of money, keep is defensible.
why.trial_video: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $147.00; contribution = 147.00 x 0.70 - 147.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $97.03 vs spend $60 -> net +$37.03 (1.62 contribution per ad dollar). Profitable on exactly 3 counted orders; a cautious increase or keep are both reasonable, never a cut.

name: Refunds wipe out the best seller
story: The trial video took twelve $49 payments, but nine were fully refunded, so the apparent top ad is really a loser.

why.trial_video: 12 payments (excluded: 9 fully refunded) -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $147.00; contribution = 147.00 x 0.70 - 147.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $97.03 vs spend $150 -> net -$52.97 (0.65 contribution per ad dollar). Gross $588 would look like a winner, but after 9 full refunds it loses money and a 75% refund rate says the ad attracts the wrong buyers: reduce or pause, never increase.
why.parent_carousel: 4 payments -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $396.00; contribution = 396.00 x 0.70 - 396.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $263.40 vs spend $90 -> net +$173.40 (2.93 contribution per ad dollar). Four clean $99 orders, about three dollars of contribution per ad dollar: move budget here.

name: Partial refunds and a double payment
story: The $99 kit bundle had $80 refunded on four of five orders, and one free-guide buyer paid twice within four minutes.

why.free_guide: 3 payments (excluded: 1 duplicate) -> 2 counted orders, paid revenue $118.00; contribution = 118.00 x 0.70 - 118.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 2 = $78.09 vs spend $50 -> net +$28.09 (1.56 contribution per ad dollar). The second $59 is the same payer 4 minutes later, a double payment, so only 2 real orders: too thin to scale or cut even though it is in profit, keep.
why.holiday_static: 5 payments -> 5 counted orders, incl. 4 partly refunded, paid revenue $175.00; contribution = 175.00 x 0.70 - 175.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 5 = $114.82 vs spend $160 -> net -$45.18 (0.72 contribution per ad dollar). Gross $495 would show a healthy profit, but the partial refunds leave $175 of real revenue and the ad loses money: cut it.
why.parent_carousel: 4 payments -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $596.00; contribution = 596.00 x 0.70 - 596.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $397.42 vs spend $100 -> net +$297.42 (3.97 contribution per ad dollar). Four clean $149 orders, about four dollars of contribution per ad dollar: increase.

name: Open disputes hold back the money
story: Two of the trial video's four payments are in open disputes, while the carousel's $199 orders are strong even with its one dispute set aside.

why.trial_video: 4 payments (excluded: 2 in open dispute) -> 2 counted orders, paid revenue $98.00; contribution = 98.00 x 0.70 - 98.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 2 = $64.69 vs spend $100 -> net -$35.31 (0.65 contribution per ad dollar). Counting the disputed money it would look profitable on 4 orders, but only 2 are settled: too thin to act on, keep until the disputes resolve.
why.parent_carousel: 5 payments (excluded: 1 in open dispute) -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $796.00; contribution = 796.00 x 0.70 - 796.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $531.44 vs spend $220 -> net +$311.44 (2.42 contribution per ad dollar). Even with the disputed $199 set aside, four settled orders return over two dollars per ad dollar: increase.
why.free_guide: 0 payments, 0 counted orders, contribution $0.00 vs spend $60, net -$60. 30 leads and no payments at all: too few orders to judge (keep), and checking that its clicks are attributed to PayPal payments (fix_tracking) is equally sensible.

name: Too few orders to call
story: Every ad has only one or two paid orders this week, including a $199 ad that looks hugely profitable and a $19 ad that looks hopeless.

why.trial_video: 1 payments -> 1 counted orders, paid revenue $49.00; contribution = 49.00 x 0.70 - 49.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 1 = $32.34 vs spend $45 -> net -$12.66 (0.72 contribution per ad dollar). One order is no evidence either way: keep.
why.holiday_static: 2 payments -> 2 counted orders, paid revenue $398.00; contribution = 398.00 x 0.70 - 398.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 2 = $265.72 vs spend $120 -> net +$145.72 (2.21 contribution per ad dollar). Two big orders make a large profit, but two sales can be luck: keep and wait for a third before scaling.
why.free_guide: 1 payments -> 1 counted orders, paid revenue $19.00; contribution = 19.00 x 0.70 - 19.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 1 = $12.24 vs spend $80 -> net -$67.76 (0.15 contribution per ad dollar). It is losing money, but a single $19 order cannot separate a bad ad from a slow week: keep for another week rather than cut.

name: All profitable, one clearly best
story: All three ads make money after costs, but the $149 carousel returns about six dollars of contribution per ad dollar, three times the others.

why.trial_video: 6 payments -> 6 counted orders, paid revenue $294.00; contribution = 294.00 x 0.70 - 294.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 6 = $194.07 vs spend $100 -> net +$94.07 (1.94 contribution per ad dollar). Solidly profitable on 6 orders: keep or increase; cutting a profitable ad would be wrong.
why.parent_carousel: 6 payments -> 6 counted orders, paid revenue $894.00; contribution = 894.00 x 0.70 - 894.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 6 = $596.13 vs spend $100 -> net +$496.13 (5.96 contribution per ad dollar). By far the best return on solid evidence: extra money should go here first.
why.free_guide: 5 payments -> 5 counted orders, paid revenue $195.00; contribution = 195.00 x 0.70 - 195.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 5 = $128.22 vs spend $80 -> net +$48.22 (1.60 contribution per ad dollar). Profitable but the weakest of the three: keep (or a modest increase), not a cut.

name: Every ad loses after costs
story: Two of the three ads bring in more revenue than their ad spend, yet after the 30% cost and fees every ad loses money, and the $19 guide loses most of its budget.

why.trial_video: 4 payments -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $196.00; contribution = 196.00 x 0.70 - 196.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $129.38 vs spend $150 -> net -$20.62 (0.86 contribution per ad dollar). Revenue/spend 1.31 but it returns under a dollar per ad dollar after costs: cut it.
why.free_guide: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $57.00; contribution = 57.00 x 0.70 - 57.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $36.73 vs spend $150 -> net -$113.27 (0.24 contribution per ad dollar). $19 orders return about 24 cents per ad dollar, so every dollar spent loses about 76 cents: pause; a mere reduction keeps burning money.
why.parent_carousel: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $297.00; contribution = 297.00 x 0.70 - 297.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $197.55 vs spend $250 -> net -$52.45 (0.79 contribution per ad dollar). Revenue/spend 1.19 and it loses money on the biggest budget: cut it; no ad deserves an increase this week.

name: The lead count tells the truth
story: The ad with the most leads also has the most sales and the best profit, while the low-lead ad loses money.

why.trial_video: 9 payments -> 9 counted orders, paid revenue $441.00; contribution = 441.00 x 0.70 - 441.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 9 = $291.10 vs spend $100 -> net +$191.10 (2.91 contribution per ad dollar). Nine clean orders and nearly three dollars of contribution per ad dollar: here the obvious answer (most leads, scale it) is right.
why.holiday_static: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $177.00; contribution = 177.00 x 0.70 - 177.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $117.14 vs spend $150 -> net -$32.86 (0.78 contribution per ad dollar). Few leads and a loss after costs: move money away from it.

name: Low ticket fees, thin big ticket, missing payments
story: A $19 guide sells a lot but costs and the per-order fee sink it, a $199 ad has only two sales, the carousel shows leads but no payments, and the trial video has a double payment and a partial refund.

why.free_guide: 12 payments -> 12 counted orders, paid revenue $228.00; contribution = 228.00 x 0.70 - 228.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 12 = $146.90 vs spend $200 -> net -$53.10 (0.73 contribution per ad dollar). Twelve sales and revenue/spend 1.14 look busy, but at $19 the 30% cost plus $0.49 per order leave it losing money: cut it.
why.holiday_static: 2 payments -> 2 counted orders, paid revenue $398.00; contribution = 398.00 x 0.70 - 398.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 2 = $265.72 vs spend $60 -> net +$205.72 (4.43 contribution per ad dollar). Very profitable on paper, but two orders is too thin to scale: keep.
why.parent_carousel: 0 payments, 0 counted orders, contribution $0.00 vs spend $180, net -$180. 25 leads and zero recorded payments while the other ads record theirs: too thin to cut; checking that its clicks reach PayPal attribution (fix_tracking) or keeping one more week are both right.
why.trial_video: 5 payments (excluded: 1 duplicate) -> 4 counted orders, incl. 1 partly refunded, paid revenue $171.50; contribution = 171.50 x 0.70 - 171.50 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $112.96 vs spend $70 -> net +$42.96 (1.61 contribution per ad dollar). The double payment is not a second order and the half refund lowers revenue, yet it stays profitable on 4 real orders: increase or keep.
